audio.t: Good afternoon, everyone, and thanks for coming to today's exchange orientation. I'm Ms. Lin from the Office of International Affairs. First, let's talk about credits. Before you leave, you must fill out a course mapping form, and your department chair needs to sign it. If you skip this step, the courses you take overseas may not count toward your graduation requirements here.

Second, money. As exchange students, you'll keep paying tuition to our university, not to the host school. However, you are responsible for your own housing, flights, and health insurance. Many of you are eligible for the Ministry of Education's study abroad scholarship, and the application period opens on November first.

Finally, a word of advice. Students often tell me the hardest part isn't the classes. It's feeling lonely during the first month. So join a club or a language exchange as soon as you arrive. Next week, three students who just came back from Sweden, Korea, and Canada will share their experiences, and I strongly encourage you to attend.

questions.explain: 講者說出國前須填課程對應表並由系主任簽名，否則學分可能不被承認，故選 D。學費仍繳給本校，A 錯；B、C 未提及。

head: From: Office of International Affairs <oia@univ.edu.tw>
To: Spring 2027 Exchange Applicants
Subject: Interview Schedule and Required Documents
passage: Thank you for applying to the Spring 2027 exchange program. All applicants who passed the document review will be invited to a fifteen-minute interview, which will take place from November 16 to 18. Your individual time slot will be posted on the OIA website by November 10.

The interview will be conducted mainly in English, so please be ready to explain why you chose your top three partner schools and how the experience fits your academic plans. If you have a class conflict, you may request a different time slot by emailing us no later than November 12. Requests received after this date cannot be **accommodated**.
Please also bring your original transcript and a printed copy of your study plan. Applicants who miss the interview without notice will be considered to have withdrawn from the program.

Best regards,
Office of International Affairs

questions.explain: 全文說明面試日期、時段公告、改期方式與須攜帶文件，故選 B。結果尚未公布，也未提到新姊妹校或繳費。

To give details about the upcoming interviews

passage: For years, a full semester overseas was the standard exchange experience for students at our university. This year, however, the Office of International Affairs (OIA) reports that applications for short-term programs, such as summer schools, four-week language courses, and winter field trips, have risen by nearly forty percent, while applications for semester-long exchanges have stayed about the same.

OIA director Dr. Chen Mei-hua believes cost is the main reason. "A semester in Europe can cost a student more than three hundred thousand NT dollars once you add rent, flights, and daily expenses," she explained. "A four-week program costs a fraction of that, and students don't have to delay graduation." Many students also worry that courses taken abroad will not transfer, especially in departments with strict required courses, such as engineering and nursing.

Not everyone sees the trend as entirely positive. Professor David Morris of the Department of Foreign Languages argues that short programs rarely give students enough time to move beyond the "tourist stage." "In the first month, everything is exciting and new. The real learning, like solving problems on your own and building friendships with local students, usually happens later," he said.

To respond to these concerns, the OIA plans to launch a hybrid option next fall. Students will take an online course taught by a partner university during the semester and then spend three weeks on that campus in the summer. The office has also promised to publish a list of pre-approved overseas courses so that students can check whether their credits will transfer before they apply.

questions.explain: 首段即點出短期海外課程申請人數大增，全文圍繞此趨勢的原因與回應，故選 B。其餘選項只是細節或未提及。
options: A new scholarship for engineering students
The growing interest in short-term study abroad programs
Problems between the university and its partner schools
How to apply for a semester-long exchange
